# Apollo

> Apollo is the open source brain for physical agents. It runs as a worker on infrastructure you own and drives a physical device that has a mic, a speaker, and a face. It does not live in a chat window: you say its name out loud and the answer comes back spoken.

Apollo ships the brain, not the body. You bring a device, flash open firmware onto it, and pick the wake word it answers to. Any client that speaks the Apollo protocol is a valid body. Apollo is MIT licensed and free, and it is built by Valentín Galfre (github.com/galfrevn).

## What it does

- Voice turns: it answers out loud in short sentences, with nothing to read or type
- Memory: it keeps what you tell it and brings it back when it fits, even weeks later
- Reminders: timers and scheduled alerts that fire on the body itself
- Live answers: it searches the web and gives you the answer, not a list of links
- Coding agent: it works on your repository in a sandbox and reports how it went
- Your tools: your calendar, notes, and other services connected over MCP
- Character: its name, its voice, and four speech modes that each carry their own face

## Architecture

The body streams audio to the brain, which owns every turn, the memory, the schedules, and the character. Swapping the body changes nothing, because no state lives on it. Today the brain deploys to Cloudflare as a Durable Object per body; that is the current target rather than a permanent dependency.

## Handbook chapters

- [Purpose](https://heyapollo.dev/docs/purpose): What Apollo is and is not.
- [Concepts](https://heyapollo.dev/docs/concepts): Desk, turns, sessions, and tools.
- [Loop](https://heyapollo.dev/docs/loop): How a request becomes a spoken reply.
- [Protocol](https://heyapollo.dev/docs/protocol): The full wire contract between the device and the server.
- [Capabilities](https://heyapollo.dev/docs/capabilities): Every tool Apollo can reach, and when it asks first.
- [Setup](https://heyapollo.dev/docs/setup): From one command to a deployed, talking worker.
- [Console](https://heyapollo.dev/docs/console): Manage a deployment from the browser.
- [Skills](https://heyapollo.dev/docs/skills): Hand the manual to your coding agent.
- [Firmware](https://heyapollo.dev/docs/firmware): Build, flash, and point a body at your brain.
- [Roadmap](https://heyapollo.dev/docs/roadmap): Where Apollo is going next.
